title: EKS: human access with IAM and access entries
summary: Users authenticate with their IAM identity, usually an IAM Identity Center permission-set role. An EKS access entry maps that role into the cluster and attaches an access policy, at cluster or namespace scope.
notes: Authentication: aws eks get-token creates a pre-signed STS GetCallerIdentity request, and EKS verifies who you are from it. No Kubernetes passwords or certificates.
Access entries (EKS API) replace the old aws-auth ConfigMap. They are managed through IAM-controlled API calls and audited in CloudTrail, and a bad edit can't lock everyone out.
Map the permission-set role, not individual users. Identity Center role ARNs contain a random suffix, so manage the entries with IaC.
The cluster creator gets cluster-admin by default. Turn that off (bootstrapClusterCreatorAdminPermissions=false) and grant admin deliberately.
